title: Open Values Challenge Index v0.1
description: A compact version of the challenge set for sites to read: each worked example with its top picks recomputed from the current category data and the chosen sourced facts filled in. pipeline/build_challenge.js builds it from content/challenge/index.json into app/data/challenge-index.json; change the challenge set, not this file.

format.description: Always "open-values-challenge-index". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the index format this file follows. Must start with 0.1.0.

standard.description: Always "open-values-standard", the standard this format belongs to.

built.description: The date of the challenge set this index was built from, copied from that file's updated field, as YYYY-MM-DD.

purpose.description: A sentence saying what this index is for.

generatedFrom.description: The challenge set file this index was built from, its date, and its hash, so anyone can check the index against it.

counts.description: How many sites, methods, cases, contrary tags and categories the challenge set holds.

principles.description: Copied unchanged from the challenge set: the rules challenge features follow.

algorithms.description: The methods from the challenge set, with only their id, label and summary.

instances.description: The sites and apps from the challenge set, copied with their settings.

categories.description: Every category that has at least one case, sorted by id, with its criteria.

cases.description: Every case from the challenge set, with each view reranked against the current category data and the chosen sourced facts filled in.

path.description: Always "content/challenge/index.json", the file this index is built from.

updated.description: The challenge set's own updated date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 hash of the challenge set file text at build time, in 64 lowercase hex characters.

instances.description: How many sites and apps are listed.

contraryTags.description: How many contrary tags the challenge set holds.

categories.description: How many different categories the cases cover.

note.description: One or two sentences saying what the source shows.

source.description: The web address of the source, starting with http:// or https://.

asof.description: When the source was checked, as a year such as "2026", or a year and month such as "2026-08".

tag.description: The id of the contrary tag, such as "ai-assistants/jan-ai/safety".

axis.description: The criterion key the fact is about, such as "safety".

score.description: The entry's score on that criterion, from 0 to 100.

additionalProperties.description: The weight for one criterion, from 0 (ignored) to 5 (counts most).

code.description: The code of the entry that ranks first, as it appears in the category dataset.

name.description: The name of that entry, such as "Jan".

brand.description: A short tag the dataset gives the entry, such as "local open-source assistant".

score.description: The entry's overall fit under this weighting, from 0 to 100, as the app's scoring engine computes it.

coverage.description: The share of the weighting that the entry has scores for, from 0 to 1, rounded to four places. 1 means every weighted criterion has a score.

why.description: The labels of the criteria that added the most to the score, at most two, such as "Privacy".

id.description: A short name for the method, such as "opposite-view" or "steelman".

label.description: The name to show readers, such as "Opposite view".

summary.description: One or two sentences saying what the method does.

id.description: A short name for the site or app, such as "kosplora".

label.description: The name to show readers, such as "Kosplora".

role.description: What part the site plays for challenge features, as a short label such as "flagship-learning-instance".

status.description: How far along the site is, when it is not yet live, such as "format-seed".

challengeDefault.description: How visible the challenge feature is by default on this site: available (there if asked for), prominent (shown alongside results), or primary (the main thing the site shows).

surfaces.description: The places on the site where a challenge can appear, such as "verdict", "category" or "entry".

label.description: The category name shown to readers, such as "AI assistants".

type.description: What kind of thing the category covers: Products, Services, Media, Organizations, or Initiatives.

file.description: The path of the category dataset, such as "app/data/ai-assistants.json".

n.description: How many entries the category dataset holds.

criteria.description: The criteria entries in the category are scored on, in dataset order.

key.description: The criterion key used in weights and scores, such as "privacy".

label.description: The criterion name shown to readers, such as "Privacy".
A short name for the weighting, such as "Privacy and openness first".

weights.description: How much each criterion counts in this view, keyed by criterion key from the category dataset, such as { "privacy": 5, "safety": 2 }. Each weight runs from 0 (ignored) to 5 (counts most).

expectedTop.description: The code of the entry the challenge set says this weighting ranks first.

top.description: The entry that actually ranks first under this weighting when the index is built. It should match expectedTop.

sourceTag.description: For the opposite view, the id of the contrary tag that backs its top pick.

selectedTag.description: For the opposite view, the contrary tag the builder chose: the highest-scoring opposite-view-strength fact for the top pick.

receipt.description: The same fact as selectedTag, repeated under this name for display code that reads it.

forEntity.description: The code of the entry the weakness is about, the user view's top pick.

axis.description: The criterion key the weakness is on, such as "safety".

sourceTag.description: The id of the contrary tag that backs the weakness.

framing.description: The sentence a reader sees about the weakness.

line.description: The same sentence as framing, repeated under this name for display code that reads it.

selectedTag.description: The contrary tag the builder chose: the lowest-scoring steelman-weakness fact for the top pick on a criterion the user view weights at 2 or below.

receipt.description: The same fact as selectedTag, repeated under this name for display code that reads it.

id.description: A unique name for this case, in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

category.description: The id of the category dataset the case ranks, such as "ai-assistants".

label.description: A short title for the case, such as "Open/local AI assistant versus managed safety".

reads.description: The one sentence a reader sees, 24 to 140 characters. The challenge audit requires it to start with "The strongest case the other way: ".

userView.description: The weighting a reader is likely to hold, the entry it is expected to put on top, and the entry that actually ranks first.

oppositeView.description: The opposite weighting, its expected and actual top pick, and the sourced fact that backs that pick.

steelman.description: The strongest sourced weakness of the user view's top pick, on a criterion that view barely weights.
